title: Grids That Guide Earth's Balance
subject: Social Science
description: Understand the imaginary grid of latitudes and longitudes that helps us locate places, understand climate zones, and read time across the globe — from the Equator and Prime Meridian to the Tropics, Polar Circles, and the story of the longitude problem.

questions.question: What are latitudes?
options: Imaginary lines running east to west around the Earth
Imaginary lines running north to south connecting the poles
Real physical lines drawn on the ground
Lines that only appear on globes, never on maps
questions.explanation: Latitudes are imaginary lines that run east to west around the Earth.

questions.question: What do lines of latitude help us understand?
options: How far north or south a place is from the Equator
How far east or west a place is
The exact population of a place
The colour of the soil in a region
questions.explanation: Latitudes tell us how far north or south a place is from the Equator.

questions.question: What is the Equator?
options: The imaginary line at 0° latitude around the middle of the Earth
The line where the date changes
A line that runs from pole to pole
A line only found in the Arctic region
questions.explanation: The Equator is the imaginary line at 0° latitude that runs around the middle of the Earth.

questions.question: What two hemispheres does the Equator divide the Earth into?
options: Northern and Southern Hemisphere
Eastern and Western Hemisphere
Hot and Cold Hemisphere
Land and Water Hemisphere
questions.explanation: The Equator divides the Earth into the Northern and Southern Hemispheres.

questions.question: Latitude degrees range from 0° at the Equator to how many degrees at the poles?
questions.explanation: Latitude is measured in degrees from 0° at the Equator to 90° at the poles.

questions.question: The Equator is the longest and most important line of latitude.
questions.explanation: The Equator is the longest line of latitude and the most important reference line for measuring latitude.

questions.question: Why does the Equator have a warm, humid climate all year round?
options: It receives direct, strong sunlight throughout the year
It is located at 90° latitude, far from the sun
It receives sunlight only in winter
It never receives any sunlight at all
questions.explanation: The Equator faces the sun directly, so it receives strong, direct sunlight all year, giving it a warm and humid climate.

questions.question: Which of these countries lies on or near the Equator, according to the chapter?
options: Kenya
Norway
Russia
Canada
questions.explanation: Kenya is one of the countries mentioned in the chapter as lying on or near the Equator.

questions.question: Select ALL countries mentioned in the chapter as lying on or near the Equator.
options: Brazil
Kenya
Indonesia
Norway
questions.explanation: Brazil, Kenya, and Indonesia are the countries mentioned as lying on or near the Equator. Norway is far from the Equator, near the Arctic Circle.

questions.question: Why is the Equator used as the starting point (0°) for measuring all latitude?
options: It provides a clear, fixed reference line to measure how far north or south any place is
It is the coldest place on Earth
It is the only place where the sun ever shines
It was chosen randomly with no real reason
questions.explanation: The Equator is used as the 0° starting point because it gives a clear, fixed reference for measuring how far north or south any place is.

questions.question: As you move away from the Equator toward the poles, what generally happens to the climate?
options: It generally becomes colder
It generally becomes warmer
It stays exactly the same everywhere
It becomes wetter but never colder
questions.explanation: As you move away from the Equator toward the poles, the climate generally becomes colder.

questions.question: Places near the Equator are generally warmer than places near the poles.
questions.explanation: Places near the Equator receive more direct sunlight and are generally warmer than places near the poles.

questions.question: Why are places near the Equator warmer than places near the poles?
options: They receive more direct sunlight throughout the year
They are located at a higher latitude number
They receive no sunlight at all
They are always covered in snow
questions.explanation: Places near the Equator receive more direct sunlight throughout the year, making them warmer than places near the poles.

questions.question: Lines of latitude run in which general direction?
options: East to West
North to South
Diagonally only
They have no direction
questions.explanation: Lines of latitude run east to west around the Earth.

questions.question: If a place has a latitude close to 0°, what can you infer about its likely climate?
options: It is likely warm, since it is close to the Equator
It is likely very cold, since it is close to the poles
It is impossible to guess anything about its climate
It must be located in the Arctic Circle
questions.explanation: A latitude close to 0° means the place is near the Equator, so it is likely to have a warm climate.

questions.question: Which of these two places would likely be warmer: a place at 5°S latitude or a place at 60°N latitude?
options: The place at 5°S, since it is much closer to the Equator
The place at 60°N, since it has a bigger number
Both places would be equally warm
It is impossible to know without more information
questions.explanation: A place at 5°S is much closer to the Equator (0°) than a place at 60°N, so it is likely to be warmer.

questions.question: What is the value of latitude exactly at the North Pole?
questions.explanation: The North Pole is located at 90°N latitude.

questions.question: What is the value of latitude exactly at the South Pole?
questions.explanation: The South Pole is located at 90°S latitude.

questions.question: Latitude values increase as you move from the Equator toward either pole.
questions.explanation: Latitude values increase from 0° at the Equator to 90° at either pole.

questions.question: Why do we say latitude 'measures how far north or south' a place is, rather than 'how far east or west'?
options: Because latitude lines run east-west, and moving between them changes your north-south position
Because latitude lines run north-south, changing your east-west position
Because latitude has nothing to do with position at all
Because latitude only applies to the Southern Hemisphere
questions.explanation: Since latitude lines run east-west (like rings around the Earth), moving between different latitude lines changes how far north or south you are.

questions.question: Which of these is the correct order of latitude value, from smallest to largest?
options: Equator, Tropic of Cancer, Arctic Circle, North Pole
North Pole, Arctic Circle, Tropic of Cancer, Equator
Arctic Circle, Equator, Tropic of Cancer, North Pole
Tropic of Cancer, North Pole, Equator, Arctic Circle
questions.explanation: In order from smallest to largest latitude: Equator (0°), Tropic of Cancer (23.5°N), Arctic Circle (66.5°N), North Pole (90°N).

questions.question: Which of these places would be located at a HIGHER latitude number: a place near the North Pole or a place near the Equator?
options: A place near the North Pole
A place near the Equator
Both are always the same
Latitude does not apply near poles
questions.explanation: A place near the North Pole would have a higher latitude number (closer to 90°) than a place near the Equator (closer to 0°).

questions.question: According to the chapter's ocean grid activity, in which grid square was the whale hiding?
options: C5
A1
E1
B2
questions.explanation: In the ocean grid activity, the whale was hiding at C5.

questions.question: In the chapter's ocean grid activity, which sea creature was found at grid square E1?
options: Shark
Boat
Turtle
Dolphin
questions.explanation: The shark was found at grid square E1 in the ocean grid activity.

questions.question: In the chapter's ocean grid activity, the turtle's correct address was B3.
questions.explanation: The turtle's correct address in the ocean grid activity was A4, not B3.

questions.question: What is the purpose of a coordinate grid, like the one used in the ocean activity with letters and numbers?
options: It helps locate an exact position by combining a row and a column reference
It only shows colours, with no location information
It is used only for measuring temperature
It has no real-world equivalent, unlike latitude and longitude
questions.explanation: A coordinate grid, like letters and numbers on the ocean activity, helps locate an exact position by combining a row and a column reference — similar to how latitude and longitude work together.

questions.question: Every place on Earth has its own latitude and longitude 'address.' What does Mumbai's latitude and longitude help identify?
options: Its exact location on Earth
Its population size
Its currency
Its national language
questions.explanation: A place's latitude and longitude together act like an address that helps identify its exact location on Earth.

questions.question: Given a place's coordinates like '18.9°N, 72.8°E,' which number represents its latitude?
options: Both numbers equally
Neither number represents latitude
questions.explanation: The first number, 18.9°N, represents the latitude, showing how far north of the Equator the place is.

questions.question: What does the 'N' in a latitude value like '18.9°N' tell you?
options: The place is north of the Equator
The place is south of the Equator
The place is east of the Prime Meridian
The place is west of the Prime Meridian
questions.explanation: The 'N' in a latitude value like 18.9°N tells you the place is located north of the Equator.

questions.question: What does the 'S' in a latitude value like '23.5°S' tell you?
options: The place is south of the Equator
The place is north of the Equator
The place is on the Equator
The place is at the North Pole
questions.explanation: The 'S' in a latitude value tells you the place is located south of the Equator.

questions.question: Why do we need a system of latitudes at all?
options: To measure and describe how far north or south a place is on Earth
To measure the height of mountains only
To calculate the population of countries
To calculate ocean depth
questions.explanation: The system of latitudes exists to measure and describe how far north or south a place is on Earth.

questions.question: Latitude lines are imaginary, not real physical lines drawn on the Earth.
questions.explanation: Latitude lines are imaginary lines used to help us understand and describe location; they are not real physical lines.

questions.question: Why is it important that latitude lines are described as 'imaginary'?
options: It clarifies that they are conceptual tools for measuring position, not physical markings on Earth
It means latitude lines have no real use at all
It means only satellites can see latitude lines
It means latitude lines change position every day
questions.explanation: Describing latitude lines as 'imaginary' clarifies that they are conceptual tools for measuring position, not physical markings that actually exist on the ground.

questions.question: Which of these best describes latitude?
options: A measurement of a place's position north or south of the Equator
A measurement of a place's population
A measurement of a place's average rainfall
A measurement of a country's total land area
questions.explanation: Latitude is a measurement of a place's position north or south of the Equator.

questions.question: A place located at 45°N is roughly halfway between which two reference lines?
options: The Equator (0°) and the North Pole (90°N)
The Equator (0°) and the South Pole (90°S)
The Arctic Circle and Antarctic Circle only
The Tropic of Cancer and Tropic of Capricorn only
questions.explanation: A place at 45°N is roughly halfway between the Equator (0°) and the North Pole (90°N).

questions.question: Why can't a single latitude line, by itself, tell you the exact location of a place on Earth?
options: A latitude line only tells you how far north/south you are — you also need longitude for east/west position
A single latitude line already gives you the complete exact address
Latitude lines don't actually provide any location information
Only longitude is ever needed to find an exact place
questions.explanation: A latitude line only tells you how far north or south a place is; you also need longitude to know the exact location, since it shows east-west position.

questions.question: Which is TRUE about the number of latitude degrees at the Equator?
options: It is 0°
It is 90°
It is 180°
It is 45°
questions.explanation: The Equator is located at 0° latitude.

questions.question: Which best explains why latitude is useful for understanding climate?
options: Places at different latitudes receive different amounts of direct sunlight, affecting temperature
Latitude has no connection to temperature or climate
All latitudes receive exactly the same amount of sunlight
Only longitude affects a place's climate
questions.explanation: Latitude is useful for understanding climate because places at different latitudes receive different amounts of direct sunlight, which affects temperature.

questions.question: All places on Earth receive exactly the same amount of sunlight, regardless of latitude.
questions.explanation: Places at different latitudes receive different amounts of direct sunlight, which is why climates vary from the Equator to the poles.

questions.question: Which best summarizes what latitude tells us about a place?
options: How far north or south of the Equator a place is located
How far east or west of the Prime Meridian a place is located
How large a place's population is
How much rainfall a place receives each year
questions.explanation: Latitude tells us how far north or south of the Equator a place is located.

questions.question: What is the Tropic of Cancer?
options: A line of latitude at 23.5°N
A line of latitude at 23.5°S
A line of longitude at 23.5°E
The line where the date changes
questions.explanation: The Tropic of Cancer is a line of latitude located at 23.5°N.

questions.question: What is the Tropic of Capricorn?
options: A line of latitude at 23.5°S
A line of latitude at 23.5°N
A line of longitude at 23.5°W
The line where time zones begin
questions.explanation: The Tropic of Capricorn is a line of latitude located at 23.5°S.

questions.question: What is the region between the Tropic of Cancer and the Tropic of Capricorn called?
options: The Tropical Zone
The Polar Zone
The Temperate Zone
The Frigid Zone
questions.explanation: The region between the Tropic of Cancer and the Tropic of Capricorn is called the Tropical Zone.

questions.question: What kind of climate is typically found in the Tropical Zone?
options: Warm, lush, with rainforests and heavy rainfall
Cold and snowy year-round
Extremely dry with no rainfall at all
Freezing with 24-hour darkness
questions.explanation: The Tropical Zone typically has a warm, lush climate with rainforests and heavy rainfall.

questions.question: Which Indian states does the Tropic of Cancer pass through, according to the chapter?
options: Gujarat, Madhya Pradesh, Jharkhand, and Mizoram
Punjab, Haryana, Delhi, and Rajasthan
Kerala, Tamil Nadu, and Karnataka
Jammu & Kashmir and Himachal Pradesh
questions.explanation: The chapter states that the Tropic of Cancer passes through Gujarat, Madhya Pradesh, Jharkhand, and Mizoram in India.

questions.question: The Tropic of Cancer passes through India.
questions.explanation: The Tropic of Cancer passes through several Indian states, including Gujarat, Madhya Pradesh, Jharkhand, and Mizoram.

questions.question: Why does the Tropical Zone (between the two Tropics) tend to be warm and rainy?
options: It is close to the Equator and receives strong, direct sunlight for most of the year
It is closest to the North Pole
It receives no sunlight throughout the year
It is located inside the Arctic Circle
questions.explanation: The Tropical Zone is close to the Equator and receives strong, direct sunlight for most of the year, making it warm and rainy.

questions.question: A place is located between the Tropic of Cancer and the Tropic of Capricorn. What kind of climate would you expect there?
options: Warm and possibly rainforest-like
Extremely cold with polar night
Covered in ice year-round
Experiencing 24 hours of darkness in winter
questions.explanation: A place located within the Tropical Zone (between the two Tropics) would generally have a warm, rainforest-like climate.

questions.question: Which line of latitude is located exactly at 23.5° north of the Equator?
options: Tropic of Cancer
Tropic of Capricorn
Arctic Circle
Antarctic Circle
questions.explanation: The Tropic of Cancer is located exactly at 23.5° north of the Equator.

questions.question: Which line of latitude is located exactly at 23.5° south of the Equator?
options: Tropic of Capricorn
Tropic of Cancer
Arctic Circle
Antarctic Circle
questions.explanation: The Tropic of Capricorn is located exactly at 23.5° south of the Equator.

questions.question: Raj lives in India, where the Tropic of Cancer passes through his country. Based on this, what is India's climate near this line likely to be?
options: Warm, since it is close to the Equator
Extremely cold, similar to the Arctic
Covered in ice year-round
Experiencing polar night for months
questions.explanation: Since the Tropic of Cancer is relatively close to the Equator, areas near it, like parts of India, tend to have a warm climate.

questions.question: Mateo lives in Brazil, at a location around 15°S latitude. Where does this place him relative to the Tropics?
options: Within the Tropical Zone, between the Equator and Tropic of Capricorn
North of the Arctic Circle
Exactly at the South Pole
West of the Prime Meridian only, with no latitude information
questions.explanation: A location at 15°S falls within the Tropical Zone, between the Equator (0°) and the Tropic of Capricorn (23.5°S).

questions.question: The Tropic of Cancer and Tropic of Capricorn are both located at the same distance (23.5°) from the Equator, but in opposite directions.
questions.explanation: The Tropic of Cancer is 23.5°N and the Tropic of Capricorn is 23.5°S — the same distance from the Equator, but in opposite directions.

questions.question: Which of these Indian states is NOT mentioned in the chapter as being crossed by the Tropic of Cancer?
options: Kerala
Gujarat
Madhya Pradesh
Jharkhand
questions.explanation: Kerala is not mentioned in the chapter; the Tropic of Cancer is described as passing through Gujarat, Madhya Pradesh, Jharkhand, and Mizoram.

questions.question: Which term describes the warm region located between the Tropic of Cancer and Tropic of Capricorn?
options: Tropical Zone
Polar Zone
Frigid Zone
Time Zone
questions.explanation: The warm region between the Tropic of Cancer and Tropic of Capricorn is called the Tropical Zone.

questions.question: Why might rainforests commonly be found within the Tropical Zone?
options: The warm climate and heavy rainfall in this zone support lush plant growth
The Tropical Zone is always freezing and dry
Rainforests only grow near the poles
The Tropical Zone receives the least sunlight on Earth
questions.explanation: The warm climate and heavy rainfall typical of the Tropical Zone create ideal conditions for rainforests to grow.

questions.question: If a place is located at 23.5°N exactly, which important latitude line is it on?
options: Tropic of Cancer
Tropic of Capricorn
Arctic Circle
Equator
questions.explanation: A place located at exactly 23.5°N is on the Tropic of Cancer.

questions.question: If a place is located at 23.5°S exactly, which important latitude line is it on?
options: Tropic of Capricorn
Tropic of Cancer
Antarctic Circle
Equator
questions.explanation: A place located at exactly 23.5°S is on the Tropic of Capricorn.

questions.question: Why are the Tropic of Cancer and Tropic of Capricorn considered important reference lines on Earth?
options: They mark the boundaries of the warm Tropical Zone around the Equator
They mark the coldest regions on Earth
They mark where the date changes each day
They mark the exact location of the poles
questions.explanation: The Tropic of Cancer and Tropic of Capricorn mark the boundaries of the warm Tropical Zone surrounding the Equator.

questions.question: How many degrees away from the Equator are the Tropic of Cancer and Tropic of Capricorn located?
questions.explanation: Both the Tropic of Cancer and Tropic of Capricorn are located 23.5° away from the Equator.

questions.question: The Tropic of Capricorn is located south of the Equator.
questions.explanation: The Tropic of Capricorn is located at 23.5°S, which is south of the Equator.

questions.question: The Tropic of Cancer is located south of the Equator.
questions.explanation: The Tropic of Cancer is located at 23.5°N, which is north of the Equator, not south.

questions.question: A student is told a place is 'inside the Tropical Zone.' What does this tell them about the place's likely latitude?
options: Its latitude is between 23.5°S and 23.5°N
Its latitude is exactly 90°N
Its latitude is exactly 66.5°S
Its latitude cannot be determined at all
questions.explanation: Being 'inside the Tropical Zone' means the place's latitude is between 23.5°S and 23.5°N (the two Tropics).

questions.question: Compare a place at 10°N to a place at 40°N. Which is more likely to be inside the Tropical Zone?
options: The place at 10°N
The place at 40°N
Both are equally likely
Neither is ever inside the Tropical Zone
questions.explanation: The Tropical Zone extends only to 23.5°N, so a place at 10°N is inside it, while a place at 40°N is not.

questions.question: Which best explains why places within the Tropical Zone rarely experience very cold winters?
options: They remain relatively close to the Equator throughout the year, keeping temperatures warm
They are located at the poles for part of the year
They receive no sunlight for six months each year
They are always covered in snow and ice
questions.explanation: Places within the Tropical Zone stay relatively close to the Equator, so they remain warm and rarely experience very cold winters.

questions.question: Which of these best describes the Tropical Zone's location on Earth?
options: The band of latitude around the Equator, between the two Tropics
The regions near the North and South Poles
The line where the international date changes
The area only found in the Southern Hemisphere
questions.explanation: The Tropical Zone is the band of latitude around the Equator, located between the Tropic of Cancer and Tropic of Capricorn.

questions.question: Why might farmers in the Tropical Zone often grow crops that need a lot of rainfall and warmth?
options: The Tropical Zone's warm and rainy climate suits such crops
The Tropical Zone is always cold and dry
Crops cannot grow at all in the Tropical Zone
The Tropical Zone has no rainfall at all
questions.explanation: The Tropical Zone's warm and rainy climate makes it well-suited for crops that need a lot of rainfall and warmth.

questions.question: If you traveled from the Equator directly north, which latitude line would you cross FIRST?
options: Tropic of Cancer
Arctic Circle
North Pole
Tropic of Capricorn
questions.explanation: Traveling north from the Equator, you would first cross the Tropic of Cancer (23.5°N) before reaching the Arctic Circle or North Pole.

questions.question: If you traveled from the Equator directly south, which latitude line would you cross FIRST?
options: Tropic of Capricorn
Antarctic Circle
South Pole
Tropic of Cancer
questions.explanation: Traveling south from the Equator, you would first cross the Tropic of Capricorn (23.5°S) before reaching the Antarctic Circle or South Pole.

questions.question: Why do the Tropic of Cancer and Tropic of Capricorn matter when studying world climate zones?
options: They mark the edges of the warmest climate zone on Earth
They mark where snowfall is heaviest
They have no connection to climate at all
They only matter for measuring time zones
questions.explanation: The Tropic of Cancer and Tropic of Capricorn mark the edges of the Tropical Zone, the warmest climate zone on Earth.

questions.question: What is the Arctic Circle?
options: A line of latitude at 66.5°N
A line of latitude at 66.5°S
A line of longitude at 66.5°E
The line where the date changes
questions.explanation: The Arctic Circle is a line of latitude located at 66.5°N.

questions.question: What is the Antarctic Circle?
options: A line of latitude at 66.5°S
A line of latitude at 66.5°N
A line of longitude at 66.5°W
The line dividing Eastern and Western Hemispheres
questions.explanation: The Antarctic Circle is a line of latitude located at 66.5°S.

questions.question: What kind of climate is typically found near the Arctic and Antarctic Circles?
options: Very cold, close to the poles
Very warm and tropical
Warm and rainy, like a rainforest
Mild with no seasonal change
questions.explanation: The regions near the Arctic and Antarctic Circles have very cold climates, being close to the poles.

questions.question: What is the 'Midnight Sun,' as described using Tromsø, Norway as an example?
options: A phenomenon where the sun stays visible for 24 hours during summer near the Arctic Circle
A phenomenon where it is always night-time all year
A type of aurora seen only in winter
A festival celebrated at the North Pole
questions.explanation: The 'Midnight Sun' is a phenomenon in places like Tromsø, Norway, where the sun remains visible for 24 hours during summer, near the Arctic Circle.

questions.question: What is the 'Polar Night,' as described in the chapter's example of Tromsø, Norway?
options: A period of 24-hour darkness during winter near the Arctic Circle
A period of 24-hour daylight during winter
A festival held during summer
A type of storm that only happens at the Equator
questions.explanation: The 'Polar Night' is a period of 24-hour darkness experienced during winter in places like Tromsø, Norway, near the Arctic Circle.

questions.question: Tromsø, Norway experiences 24 hours of daylight (Midnight Sun) during summer, near the Arctic Circle.
questions.explanation: Tromsø, Norway, located near the Arctic Circle, experiences the Midnight Sun — 24 hours of daylight — during summer.

questions.question: The Arctic and Antarctic Circles experience 24 hours of daylight during winter.
questions.explanation: The Arctic and Antarctic Circles experience 24 hours of daylight in summer, not winter — in winter, they experience the Polar Night (24 hours of darkness).

questions.question: According to the Milestone review, which statement about the Arctic and Antarctic Circles is FALSE?
options: They experience 24 hours of daylight during winter
They are located near the poles
They have a very cold climate
They are lines of latitude
questions.explanation: It is false that the Arctic and Antarctic Circles experience 24 hours of daylight during winter — this actually happens during summer; winter brings the Polar Night (24-hour darkness).

questions.question: Which of these is located at 66.5° SOUTH of the Equator?
options: Antarctic Circle
Arctic Circle
Tropic of Cancer
Prime Meridian
questions.explanation: The Antarctic Circle is located at 66.5°S, south of the Equator.

questions.question: The Arctic Circle is located 66.5° south of the Equator.
questions.explanation: The Arctic Circle is located 66.5° NORTH of the Equator, not south — the Antarctic Circle is the one located south.

questions.question: Emily lives in Norway, in a town at 70°N latitude. Based on this, where is her town located relative to the Arctic Circle?
options: Above (north of) the Arctic Circle
Below (south of) the Arctic Circle
Exactly on the Equator
Exactly on the Tropic of Cancer
questions.explanation: Since the Arctic Circle is at 66.5°N, a town at 70°N is located above (north of) the Arctic Circle.

questions.question: What kind of climate would you expect Emily's town in Norway (70°N) to have?
options: Very cold, since it is close to the North Pole
Very warm and tropical
Warm and rainy like a rainforest
Identical to the climate at the Equator
questions.explanation: Since Emily's town is at 70°N, well above the Arctic Circle and close to the North Pole, it would be expected to have a very cold climate.

questions.question: What kind of climate would you expect in a town located at 70°N, well above the Arctic Circle?
options: Very cold, since it is close to the North Pole
Very warm and tropical
Warm and rainy like a rainforest
Identical to the climate at the Equator
questions.explanation: A town at 70°N, above the Arctic Circle, would be expected to have a very cold climate due to its closeness to the North Pole.

questions.question: Why do regions near the poles receive less direct sunlight than regions near the Equator?
options: Sunlight hits the polar regions at a more slanted angle, spreading the light and heat over a larger area
The poles are much farther from the sun in space than the Equator
The Equator receives no sunlight at all
Polar regions are covered by clouds at all times
questions.explanation: Sunlight hits polar regions at a more slanted angle than the Equator, spreading the light and heat over a larger area and making it less intense.

questions.question: Which is TRUE about the poles (90°N and 90°S)?
options: They are the coldest regions of the Earth
They are the warmest regions of the Earth
They are located at 0° latitude
They receive the most direct sunlight
questions.explanation: The poles (90°N and 90°S) are the coldest regions of the Earth.

questions.question: During the Midnight Sun period in Tromsø, Norway, approximately how many hours of daylight occur?
options: 24 hours
12 hours
0 hours
6 hours
questions.explanation: During the Midnight Sun period, Tromsø experiences approximately 24 hours of daylight.

questions.question: During the Polar Night period in Tromsø, Norway, approximately how many hours of daylight occur?
options: 0 hours (24 hours of darkness)
24 hours
12 hours
18 hours
questions.explanation: During the Polar Night period, Tromsø experiences approximately 0 hours of daylight — 24 hours of darkness.

questions.question: Why do places near the Arctic Circle, like Tromsø, experience such extreme differences in daylight between summer and winter?
options: Their high latitude causes them to receive continuous sunlight in summer and continuous darkness in winter, due to Earth's tilt
They are located exactly on the Equator
They never receive any sunlight at all, in any season
Daylight hours are the same everywhere on Earth
questions.explanation: Places near the Arctic Circle experience extreme daylight differences due to their high latitude and the Earth's tilt, causing continuous sunlight in summer and continuous darkness in winter.

questions.question: Which region is described as experiencing 'extreme cold' beyond the Polar Circles?
options: The Polar regions near the North and South Poles
The Tropical Zone near the Equator
The area near the Prime Meridian
The region near the International Date Line
questions.explanation: The Polar regions near the North and South Poles are described as experiencing extreme cold beyond the Polar Circles.

questions.question: Which best explains why Emily's town in Norway (70°N) would have a much colder climate than Kamau's city in Kenya (near 0°)?
options: Norway is much farther from the Equator and receives less direct sunlight than Kenya
Norway receives more direct sunlight than Kenya throughout the year
Kenya is closer to the North Pole than Norway
Both places have identical climates
questions.explanation: Norway, being much farther from the Equator, receives less direct sunlight than Kenya, making its climate much colder.

questions.question: Places near the poles are generally much colder than places near the Equator.
questions.explanation: Places near the poles receive less direct sunlight and are generally much colder than places near the Equator.

questions.question: Which two lines of latitude mark where extreme cold polar climates begin?
options: Arctic Circle and Antarctic Circle
Tropic of Cancer and Tropic of Capricorn
Equator and Prime Meridian
International Date Line and Equator
questions.explanation: The Arctic Circle and Antarctic Circle mark where extreme cold polar climates begin.
